correctness.rationale: The budget slice is compact, and w -> -tL(w) is injective for t>0 by reading off the off-diagonal entries. The trace-exponential Hessian on symmetric matrices has positive exponential divided differences, including at repeated eigenvalues, so along every nonzero conductance direction it is strictly positive. Uniqueness forces invariance under pair permutations and flips, which are transitive within each class. The resulting budget is da+rb=c and the spectrum is 0, da+2b with multiplicity m, and na with multiplicity m-1 (pair-constant vectors of total sum zero). On 0<=b<=c/r, the strictly increasing derivative is mt[r exp(-t na)-(2-r) exp(-t(da+2b))]. It is positive when r>=2, including r=2. Otherwise its sign at zero gives precisely the stated threshold; if negative, its zero satisfies 2t(a-b)=log(r/(2-r)), yielding the stated positive b<c/(d+r)<c/r, so a>b>0. At equality of times the zero-conductance boundary is still the unique optimum. Under t=theta n^2/B the positive-part argument tends to 1-log(r/(2-r))/(4 theta); n^2 a/(2B) tends to one and the spending share is bounded by r/(d+r), including at the limiting boundary. These deductions are independent of sampled numerical trials.
residual_risks: Finite positive t, unnormalized Laplacian, exact linear budget and a perfect matching are essential scope conditions. The scaling statement fixes theta and r in (1,2), not varying prices near two.

originality.rationale: Finite-time exponential spectral design and activation are not distinct on their own: closely related indexed families have the same setup on other graphs. Credit here is the exact finite-time complete-graph solution, including the strict boundary convention, all-finite-time deletion at price two, and the explicit diffusive crossover. Spectral-gap antecedents for the identical geometry already establish the price-two threshold for their criterion, not the finite-time optimizer.

value.rationale: The matched complete graph gives an exactly solvable test of how a whole-spectrum diffusion design differs from slowest-mode design. The explicit positive-time transition and diffusive ratio law identify when an individually costly edge class matters, even when its spending share vanishes. The price-two equality case in particular separates a unique finite-time design from a set of gap optima. These are useful boundaries of a natural design problem, not a new general convexity theorem.
residual_risks: The value is in the complete-graph benchmark; no transfer to partially marked, normalized, heterogeneous, or discrete-time designs is established.
